### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Three distinct fixes for serving Gemma4 with NVFP4 quantization in vLLM 0.20.2: ### 1. Pipeline-parallel crash (PP > 1) When `pipeline-parallel-size > 1`, `Gemma4Model.forward` unconditionally packed `residual` and `per_layer_inputs` into `IntermediateTensors` even when both are `None`. This crashed non-first PP ranks in `sync_and_slice_intermediate_tensors` with `TypeError` (slicing `None`). **Fix**: Only include non-`None` keys in the returned `IntermediateTensors`; use `.get()` on the receive side; guard `sync_and_slice_intermediate_tensors` against `None` entries. ### 2. Missing `.get()` on IntermediateTensors `IntermediateTensors` had no `.get()` method, causing `AttributeError` during `torch.compile` tracing when optional keys were accessed. ### 3. Gated MoE intermediate padding for VLLM_CUTLASS With `tensor-parallel-size: 2` and `moe-backend: cutlass`, the `swizzle_blockscale` function pads the intermediate dimension of the NVFP4 block-scale tensor to the next multiple of 128. When this padded dimension exceeds the packed weight tensor's dimension, padding is needed. The existing code only implemented this padding for non-gated MoE (`is_act_and_mul=False`). For gated MoE (`is_act_and_mul=True`, where w13 fuses `[w1(gate), w3(up)]`), the code raised `NotImplementedError`. **Fix**: Split w13 into w1 and w3, pad each shard symmetrically by `pad_size // 2`, re-concatenate, and update `moe_config.intermediate_size_per_partition` accordingly. ## Reproduction ``` vllm serve gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --moe-backend cutlass ``` Fails with: ``` NotImplementedError: Intermediate size padding for w1 and w3, for VLLM_CUTLASS NvFp4 backend, but this is not currently supported ``` When enabling PP (>1): ``` TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable in sync_and_slice_intermediate_tensors ``` ## Root cause details ### PP crash `Gemma4DecoderLayer.forward` always returns `(hidden_states, None)` (gemma4.py:754), so `residual` is always `None` after the layer loop. The non-last-rank return path unconditionally bundled both `residual` (always None) and `per_layer_inputs` (None when PLE is disabled) into `IntermediateTensors`. ### CUTLASS intermediate padding `swizzle_blockscale()` (nvfp4_utils.py:39) rounds the intermediate dimension `M` up to the next multiple of 128: ```python M_padded = round_up(M, 128) pad_size = M_padded - w13.size(1) ``` When intermediate dimension is not aligned to 128 (e.g., Gemma4 with TP=2: `2 * intermediate_pp = 704`, `round_up(704, 128) = 768`), `pad_size > 0`. For gated MoE, w13 stores `[gate, up]` fused along dim-1. Padding the fused tensor asymmetrically would leave gate and up with different sizes. The fix pads each shard independently before re-concatenating. ## Performance note With TP=2 + VLLM_CUTLASS + NVFP4 W4A4, throughput was ~21 tok/s/gpu (medium-quality approx). This is slower than the Marlin (W4A16) path with EP, likely due to kernel maturity and data-parallel communication overhead without EP. ## Files modified | File | Change | |---|---| | `vllm/sequence.py` | Added `IntermediateTensors.get()` | | `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py` | Only ship non-None tensors in PP; use `.get()` on receive | | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` | Guard `sync_and_slice` against None values | | `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/flashinfer_fp4_moe.py` | Gated MoE intermediate padding for VLLM_CUTLASS | ## Patch See attached `gemma4-vllm-nvfp4-fixes.patch`. [gemma4-vllm-nvfp4-fixes.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27701860/gemma4-vllm-nvfp4-fixes.patch) With help from OpenCode connected to DeepSeek v4 Flash max. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Intermittent `vectorized_gather_kernel index out of bounds` in `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` (KV-cache update) during Gemma 4 31B + MTP K=3 inference — both FP8-block and NVFP4
signals.text:
### Your current environment Below I've described the result from the B300 node, I'm currently testing on. But I've seen the same error on H100 and H200 nodes as well.
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 CMake version : version 3.28.3 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-106-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True GPU 0-7 : NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103, 275 GB HBM) Nvidia driver version : 580.126.20 nvcc : Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture : x86_64 CPU(s) : 224 (2 sockets × 112 cores, 1 thread/core) Model name : Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6767P NUMA node(s) : 2 (node0=0-111, node1=112-223) ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== vllm : 0.20.2rc1.dev108+g06a60d3dd (commit 06a60d3, 2026-05-07) torch : 2.11.0+cu130 triton : 3.6.0 transformers : 5.8.0 flashinfer-python : 0.6.8.post1 deep_gemm : 2.5.0+891d57b (DeepGEMM commit 891d57b) nvidia-cublas : 13.1.0.3 nvidia-cudnn-cu13 : 9.19.0.56 nvidia-nccl-cu13 : 2.28.9 nvidia-cutlass-dsl : 4.4.2 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Running Gemma 4 31B (both `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block` and `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4`) with **MTP speculative decoding (K=3)** and **single-image multimodal inputs** in vLLM V1 on B300 (Blackwell, sm_103) intermittently crashes mid-inference with a PyTorch `vectorized_gather_kernel index out of bounds` device-side assertion. The crash surfaces inside `unified_kv_cache_update` → `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash` (i.e. in the KV cache *write* path, not the spec-decode dispatch itself), suggesting the scheduler/spec-decode layer is producing a slot mapping that contains an out-of-range block index for the new K/V tokens. Observed crash rate across our recent sweeps: **5 out of ~60 captioner runs (~8%)**, distributed across different cells / GPUs / quantizations / image batches — strongly looks like a non-deterministic edge case, not a config-specific failure. This appears to be the same family as the closed [#28785](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28785) (Qwen3-VL + NVFP4, also closed as "fixed in ToT" in Nov 2025) and structurally identical to the open [#42084](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42084) (GDN attention `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` gather OOB with spec-decode + prefix caching) and [#40756](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40756) (MTP draft tokens become `-1`, downstream crash). Our pinned commit (`06a60d3`, 2026-05-07) is past #28785's fix-in-ToT date, so #28785's remediation likely didn't cover this code path. ## Configuration that reproduces Engine config (lifted from the actual crashed run's vLLM startup log): ``` model = RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block # also reproduces on nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 quantization = compressed-tensors # (modelopt for the NVFP4 path; both reproduce) dtype = torch.bfloat16 max_seq_len = 5120 tensor_parallel_size = 1 pipeline_parallel_size = 1 gpu_memory_utilization = 0.95 enable_prefix_caching = True # default enable_chunked_prefill = True # default speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig( method='mtp', model='gg-hf-am/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant', num_spec_tokens=3, ) limit_mm_per_prompt = {"image": 1} sampling: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5, max_tokens=6144 ``` ## Minimal standalone reproducer Self-contained, no external deps beyond `vllm` / `transformers` / `Pillow`. Point `--images_dir` at any directory of ~500 JPEGs (e.g. COCO val2017). The CUDA assert fires non-deterministically inside `llm.generate`, typically somewhere between 5%–80% of the way through the batch. ```python """ Minimal reproducer for the intermittent CUDA `vectorized_gather_kernel index out of bounds` assert that fires inside vLLM V1's KV-cache write path (triton_reshape_and_cache_flash) when running Gemma 4 31B with MTP speculative decoding (K=3) on a multimodal batch. Usage ----- # FP8-block (compressed-tensors auto-detected) python vllm_repro.py --images_dir /path/to/jpegs --limit 500 # NVFP4 (modelopt loader; FP8 KV auto-applied from hf_quant_config.json) python vllm_repro.py --images_dir /path/to/jpegs \ --model nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 \ --quantization modelopt --limit 500 # Disable MTP to confirm the bug is spec-decode-gated python vllm_repro.py --images_dir /path/to/jpegs \ --num_speculative_tokens 0 --limit 500 """ import argparse from pathlib import Path from PIL import Image from transformers import AutoProcessor from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams SYSTEM_PROMPT = ( "You are an image captioner. Think briefly, then write one detailed " "paragraph describing the image.") def render_prompt(processor): messages = [ {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]}, {"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": "Caption this image."}, ]}, ] return processor.apply_chat_template( messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False, enable_thinking=True, ) def parse_args(): p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("--model", default="RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block") p.add_argument("--drafter", default="gg-hf-am/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant") p.add_argument("--quantization", default=None, help="Pass 'modelopt' for NVFP4; leave unset for FP8-block.") p.add_argument("--images_dir", required=True) p.add_argument("--max_num_seqs", type=int, default=512) p.add_argument("--max_num_batched_tokens", type=int, default=16384) p.add_argument("--num_speculative_tokens", type=int, default=3, help="MTP K. 0 disables spec decode.") p.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=500) return p.parse_args() def main(): args = parse_args() image_paths = sorted(Path(args.images_dir).glob("*.jpeg"))[:args.limit] if not image_paths: raise SystemExit(f"No *.jpeg files in {args.images_dir}") print(f"Captioning {len(image_paths)} images") processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model) prompt = render_prompt(processor=processor) speculative_config = None if args.num_speculative_tokens > 0: speculative_config = { "model": args.drafter, "num_speculative_tokens": args.num_speculative_tokens, } llm_kwargs = dict( model=args.model, max_model_len=5120, max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens=args.max_num_batched_tokens, gpu_memory_utilization=0.95, trust_remote_code=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, tensor_parallel_size=1, dtype="bfloat16", speculative_config=speculative_config, disable_log_stats=(args.num_speculative_tokens == 0), ) if args.quantization is not None: llm_kwargs["quantization"] = args.quantization llm = LLM(**llm_kwargs) sampling = SamplingParams( temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5, max_tokens=4096, ) batch = [ {"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": Image.open(p).convert("RGB")}} for p in image_paths ] # Bug fires inside this call, non-deterministically. Engine init # succeeds; first scheduler steps succeed; then mid-batch a CUDA # device-side assert fires in # vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py. outputs = llm.generate(prompts=batch, sampling_params=sampling) for path, out in zip(image_paths, outputs): print(f"--- {path.name} ---") print(out.outputs[0].text[:200]) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Our actual production runs use a longer system prompt (~3,400 tokens, `enable_thinking=true`) producing 1k–2k-token decoded captions per image — the minimal repro above shrinks the system prompt to one sentence to keep it standalone, and we've confirmed the bug fires with both the short and long prompt. ## Observed crash sites Five reproduced crashes from recent runs (all on the same B300 host, all with MTP K=3): | Run | Quant | max_num_seqs | max_num_batched_tokens | Died at | First-frame kernel | |---|---|---:|---:|---|---| | sweep cell A | FP8-block | 128 | 16384 | 243/500 | `vectorized_gather_kernel` (block.y=2) | | sweep cell B | FP8-block | 128 | 20480 | 339/500 | `vectorized_gather_kernel` | | sweep cell C | NVFP4 | 384 | 20480 | 494/500 | (`launch_pdl` frame) | | 100-image run | FP8-block | 512 | 16384 | 56/100 | `vectorized_gather_kernel` | | solo ms=768 limit=2000 | NVFP4 | 768 | 16384 | mid-run | `vectorized_gather_kernel` + `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` | The crashes happen on different cells, different GPUs (we've seen GPUs 0, 1, 4, 5), different quantizations, and different points in the run — no obvious deterministic trigger. ## Assertion + traceback The on-device assertion is always one of: ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/IndexKernelUtils.cu:16: vectorized_gather_kernel: block: [N, 2, 0], thread: [T, 0, 0] Assertion `ind >=0 && ind < ind_dim_size && "vectorized gather kernel index out of bounds"` failed. ``` The `block.y=2` index in the launch geometry — consistent across our crashes — equals `K-1` for `num_speculative_tokens=3`, which is suggestive of a per-drafted-position gather producing an OOB index for the last drafted slot. Full host-side Python traceback (Triton path is the relevant tail): ``` EngineCore encountered a fatal error. Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1129, in run_engine_core engine_core.run_busy_loop() File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1170, in run_busy_loop self._process_engine_step() File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1209, in _process_engine_step outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn() File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 473, in step_with_batch_queue exec_future = self.model_executor.execute_model(...) File ".../vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py", line 114, in execute_model output.result() File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 841, in execute_model output = self.model_runner.execute_model(...) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4114, in execute_model model_output = self._model_forward(...) File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3587, in _model_forward return self.model(...) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py", line 1364, in forward hidden_states = self.language_model.model(...) File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4.py", line 1277, in forward ... File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py", line 678, in unified_kv_cache_update attn_layer.impl.do_kv_cache_update(...) File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py", line 725, in do_kv_cache_update triton_reshape_and_cache_flash(...) File ".../vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py", line 404 reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash[grid](...) ... torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` The crash is **not** in the spec-decode dispatch itself — it's the *next* op after spec-decode dispatch, the KV-cache write that copies new tokens' K/V into the paged cache via `triton_reshape_and_cache_flash`. The most natural read: the spec-decode/scheduler layer hands `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` a `slot_mapping` containing an integer outside `[0, total_kv_blocks * block_size)`, and `vectorized_gather_kernel` (used internally by that Triton kernel to look up cache slots) trips its bounds assert. The mechanism described in #40756 — *"draft tokens become -1 with 100% acceptance rate immediately before crash"* — looks like the same root cause. The `-1` draft token id would flow into the next step's slot-mapping computation, producing an OOB slot. ## What we've tried - **Running on different GPUs** — crash distribution is across GPUs (0, 1, 4, 5), so not hardware-flake. - **Running with FP8-block vs NVFP4** — both reproduce, so not quantization-layer specific. - **Different `max_num_seqs` / `max_num_batched_tokens`** — crashes at low ms (128), mid ms (384), and high ms (512, 768). - **Different prompt versions** (3 prompt variants over the same anchor set) — all reproduce. - **Different input batches** — no single image key appears to be the trigger; crashes happen at different completion counts each time. - **Re-running crashed cells** — they typically succeed on retry, confirming non-determinism. ## Not viable for our workload - **Disabling `enable_prefix_caching`** — our production system prompt is ~3,400 tokens with ~85% prefix-cache hit rate; turning prefix caching off is a non-starter for headline throughput. Mentioning it because #42084 and #40756 both list prefix caching as a required ingredient, so we expect it's part of the bug surface. ## Asks 1. **Is this a known instance of #42084 / #40756**, or a sibling? Happy to move this reproduction to a comment there if that's more useful than a new issue. 2. **Is there a fix in flight** for the spec-decode + multimodal + chunked-prefill code path that produces invalid slot mappings — or a known-good nightly we should pin to? 3. **Would dropping MTP be the only safe path** until a fix lands? We'd lose ~50% of throughput, so we'd rather wait if a fix is days away. ## MTP acceptance stats (for sanity-checking that MTP itself is working when it doesn't crash) When MTP doesn't crash, acceptance is healthy — ruling out the "MTP is silently broken" mode (#41789): | Config | Overall accept | Per-position | |---|---:|---| | FP8-block + K=3 (avg of ~10 successful runs) | 62.4% | 0.781 / 0.608 / 0.484 | | NVFP4 + K=3 (avg of ~7 successful runs) | 60.7% | 0.768 / 0.590 / 0.462 | Thanks! ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: Qwen3.5 + --enable-lora + TP=4 fails at startup in custom_all_reduce.cuh
signals.text: ### Summary Starting the vLLM OpenAI server with a Qwen3.5 model, tensor parallel size 4, and LoRA enabled fails during engine startup unless custom all-reduce is disabled. The failure happens before any adapter is loaded; starting the server with `--enable-lora --max-lora-rank 64 --max-loras 2` is enough to hit the failing path. ### Environment - GPUs: NVIDIA H200, single node - vLLM: 0.19.0 - Python: 3.10 - Model: local Qwen3.5-9B HF checkpoint - Tensor parallel: 4 - LoRA flags: `--enable-lora --max-lora-rank 64 --max-loras 2` ### Minimal command ```bash export VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=1 python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-9B \ --served-model-name qwen35 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8899 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --trust-remote-code \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-lora \ --max-lora-rank 64 \ --max-loras 2 ``` ### Observed failure The server never opens `/v1/models`. The worker logs contain: ```text Failed: Cuda error /workspace/csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'invalid argument' Worker proc VllmWorker-3 died unexpectedly, shutting down executor. EngineCore failed to start. ... RuntimeError: cancelled ... TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for engine core processes to start. ``` ### Workaround The same model and environment start successfully when adding: ```bash --enforce-eager --disable-custom-all-reduce ``` After adding those flags, `/v1/models` returns 200 and `/v1/completions` works. ### Expected behavior Either custom all-reduce should be automatically disabled for this unsupported Qwen3.5 + LoRA + TP startup path, or startup should fail early with a clear compatibility message instead of a CUDA invalid-argument and EngineCore cancellation.

signals.title: [Bug] custom_all_reduce IPC handle fails with expandable_segments when DP>1 AND TP>1
signals.text: ## Summary With `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`, starting vllm with both DP>1 and TP>1 crashes during worker init in `custom_all_reduce.cuh:455` (`cudaIpcGetMemHandle` returns `invalid argument`). Either dim alone works. ## Environment - vllm 0.20.2 - 4× H200 (1 node) ## Repro ```bash PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 ``` ``` Failed: Cuda error custom_all_reduce.cuh:455 'invalid argument' EngineCore failed to start: Worker proc VllmWorker-* died unexpectedly ``` ## Matrix (Qwen3-0.6B, expandable_segments enabled) | DP | TP | result | |----|----|--------| | 2 | 1 | ✓ | | 1 | 2 | ✓ | | 2 | 2 | ✗ (crash as above) | Independent of `--enable-sleep-mode` (reproduced with and without it). ## Root cause (best guess) `expandable_segments` reserves virtual address ranges via `cuMemAddressReserve` and commits physical memory lazily with `cuMemMap`. The base pointer returned by `cuPointerGetAttribute(..., rangeStartAddrAttr, ...)` in `get_graph_buffer_ipc_meta` is the head of such a VA range, which is not a valid source for `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` — IPC handles require memory backed by a single `cudaMalloc`/`cuMemCreate` allocation. DP=1 or TP=1 doesn't trigger the path because cross-process IPC isn't needed. ## Workaround Drop `expandable_segments` or pass `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. ## Suggested fix PR #40812 already temporarily disables `expandable_segments` around the cumem sleep-mode pool. The `custom_all_reduce` IPC graph buffer registration needs the same treatment — either temporarily switch off expandable segments while the graph buffers are being allocated/registered, or detect the cumem-backed pointer and skip custom-all-reduce IPC fallback. @youkaichao could you take a look?

signals.title: macOS source checkout resolves to UnspecifiedPlatform (empty device_type)
signals.text: **Description:** When running vLLM from a source checkout on macOS (no `pip install`), `cpu_platform_plugin()` returns `None` because the `sys.platform.startswith("darwin")` fallback is unreachable. This causes `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname()` to select `UnspecifiedPlatform`, which has `device_type = ""`, crashing any `torch.device("")` call. **Minimal Reproducible Example:** ```python # On macOS, from a source checkout (no pip install): from vllm.platforms import current_platform print(current_platform.device_type) # "" → torch.device("") crashes ``` **Expected behavior:** `cpu_platform_plugin()` returns `"vllm.platforms.cpu.CpuPlatform"` on macOS regardless of package install state. **Actual behavior:** `RuntimeError: Device string must not be empty` **Hypothesis:** `vllm_version_matches_substr("cpu")` re-raises `PackageNotFoundError` in source checkouts. The macOS fallback (`sys.platform.startswith("darwin")`) is inside the same `try` block, so the exception skips it entirely. **Environment:** macOS (darwin), Python 3.13, source checkout without pip install.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Bug Runtime LoRA unload does not fully remove the adapter from the engine. ## Description When using `/v1/load_lora_adapter`, the adapter is registered in the OpenAI serving layer and also preloaded into the engine via `add_lora`. However, `/v1/unload_lora_adapter` currently only removes the adapter from the OpenAI serving-side registry. signals.title: [Bug]: fully-sharded fused MoE W13 LoRA uses wrong slice offset after all-gather when local LoRA rank is 1
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text I could not provide a useful collect_env.py output from this reporting machine: 1. The local checkout used for source inspection is a source-only checkout and does not have vLLM installed as a package. 2. The runtime where the failure was observed is an internal multi-node deployment; its API host is not the GPU worker runtime and cannot import the worker-side vLLM dependencies directly. The source-level issue below is present on vllm-project/vllm main at: 75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c ```
### Describe the bug `fully_sharded_loras=True` with fused MoE LoRA can compute the wrong W13 slice in the expand kernel when the local LoRA rank per TP rank is 1. This is not the same as #32235. That issue was about the fused MoE LoRA launch grid size. This issue is about the post-all-gather memory layout of the W13 intermediate and the slice offset used by the expand kernel. Affected source path on current `main`: 1. `FusedMoEWithLoRA` uses two W13 slices for gated MoE: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py#L37-L40 2. `PunicaWrapperGPU.add_lora_w13` passes both slices into one combined fused MoE LoRA call: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_gpu.py#L597-L612 3. In fully-sharded mode, the intermediate rank dimension is all-gathered before expand: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L814-L827 4. `_fused_moe_lora_expand` flattens the tensor with `.view(-1, lastdim)` and passes `slice_a_size=a_intermediate_cache1.numel() // num_slices`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L581-L657 5. The kernel computes the slice base as `cur_a_ptr = a_ptr + slice_id * slice_a_size`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py#L295 That assumes each W13 slice is stored as one contiguous block after all-gather. This assumption is false for local rank 1. Minimal stride reproducer: ```python import torch world = 16 num_slices = 2 tokens = 3 topk = 1 local_rank = 1 x = torch.empty(num_slices, tokens, topk, local_rank) input_size = tuple(x.shape) out = torch.empty((world,) + input_size) z = out.reshape((world,) + input_size).movedim(0, x.dim() - 1) z = z.reshape(input_size[: x.dim() - 1] + (input_size[-1] * world,)) print("shape:", z.shape) print("stride:", z.stride()) print("actual slice1 offset:", z.stride(0)) print("kernel-assumed slice1 offset:", z.numel() // num_slices) ``` Observed output: ```text shape: torch.Size([2, 3, 1, 16]) stride: (3, 1, 96, 6) actual slice1 offset: 3 kernel-assumed slice1 offset: 48 ``` So for `slice_id=1`, the kernel reads from `base + 48`, but the correct W3 slice starts at `base + 3`. For local rank greater than 1, PyTorch materializes a contiguous copy during the final reshape, so the same assumption can accidentally hold. Example with `local_rank=4`: ```text shape: torch.Size([2, 3, 1, 64]) stride: (192, 64, 64, 1) actual slice1 offset: 192 kernel-assumed slice1 offset: 192 ``` Expected behavior: The expand kernel should address W13 slices using the actual tensor stride/layout after all-gather, or the caller should avoid the combined two-slice path for fully-sharded W13. One safe implementation pattern is to run each W13 slice as a separate `num_slices=1` expand call in fully-sharded mode. That avoids the invalid `slice_id * (numel // num_slices)` offset entirely. Observed runtime symptom: In a TP=16, rank=16 fully-sharded fused MoE LoRA setup, the rank per TP shard is 1. The routed FusedMoE LoRA path produced non-finite first-token logits. A kernel discriminator localized the problem to combined W13; W2 and single-slice W13 paths were finite, and splitting W13 into separate one-slice expand calls removed the local-rank-1 corruption. The FP8 fused MoE LoRA path appears to repeat the same pattern: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/75fd68c7a57a2f9560919a06863ea739ab46554c/vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_fp8_op.py#L620-L668 ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues. The closest issue I found was #32235, but it covers a different fused MoE LoRA bug.

The missing dependency is never checked at startup or config validation time, so the server appears ready but is completely non-functional. This is more severe than a startup crash: users see a healthy server, `/v1/models` returns 200, and there is no indication anything is wrong until the first request arrives and returns HTTP 500. ## Steps to Reproduce **Step 1: ensure `xxhash` is not installed** ```bash pip uninstall xxhash -y ``` **Case 1: `--prefix-caching-hash-algo xxhash`** ```bash vllm serve \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 20818 \ --prefix-caching-hash-algo xxhash ``` **Case 2: `--prefix-caching-hash-algo xxhash_cbor`** ```bash vllm serve \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 20819 \ --prefix-caching-hash-algo xxhash_cbor ``` Both commands start successfully and log `Application startup complete`. Then send an inference request: ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model": "", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 8 }' ``` Every request returns HTTP 500. ## Expected Behavior One of the following should happen: 1. vLLM detects at startup or config validation time that `xxhash` is not installed and exits immediately with a clear error such as `--prefix-caching-hash-algo xxhash/xxhash_cbor requires the xxhash package. Install it via pip install xxhash.`, or 2. `xxhash` is included as a required dependency in vLLM's package metadata so it is always available when either option is used. In either case, a server that cannot process any requests must not be allowed to report itself as healthy. ## Actual Behavior Both `xxhash` and `xxhash_cbor` start up fully and pass all health checks: ``` INFO Application startup complete. INFO 127.0.0.1 - "GET /v1/models HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` But every inference request fails immediately with HTTP 500 and the following error logged in the engine: **`xxhash`** — crashes in `hashing.py:xxhash`: ``` File ".../vllm/utils/hashing.py", line 73, in xxhash return _xxhash_digest(input_bytes) ModuleNotFoundError: xxhash is required for the 'xxhash' prefix caching hash algorithms. Install it via `pip install xxhash`. ``` **`xxhash_cbor`** — crashes in `hashing.py:xxhash_cbor`: ``` File ".../vllm/utils/hashing.py", line 79, in xxhash_cbor return _xxhash_digest(input_bytes) ModuleNotFoundError: xxhash is required for the 'xxhash' prefix caching hash algorithms. Install it via `pip install xxhash`. ``` Both share the same root cause in `_xxhash_digest`, which raises `ModuleNotFoundError` only when first called at request time. The error repeats for every subsequent request and the server never recovers. ## Suggested Fix Add an explicit `import xxhash` check at config validation time when `--prefix-caching-hash-algo` is set to `xxhash` or `xxhash_cbor`, and raise a clear `ImportError` or `ValueError` before the server starts. This is consistent with how other optional dependencies are guarded elsewhere in vLLM. Alternatively, add `xxhash` as an optional but declared dependency with a clear install-time note. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Silent worker termination after long idle on dual-node `--no-ray` setup (likely `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` SIGABRT)
signals.text: ## Your current environment <details> <summary>vLLM 0.20.2rc1.dev347 nightly on ARM64 / NVIDIA GB10</summary> - vLLM: `0.20.2rc1.dev347+g9946c38b7.d20260514` (nightly built 2026-05-14) - Hardware: **2× NVIDIA GB10** (ASUS Ascent GX10, sm_121, 121 GB unified memory/node) - Interconnect: ConnectX-7 RoCE (`enp1s0f0np0` Eth, `rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0` IB) - Distributed mode: `--no-ray` (PyTorch distributed backend) with `-tp 2 --nnodes 2 --master-addr 192.168.0.72 --master-port 29501` - Model: `Intel/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-int4-AutoRound` (~98 GB/node weight footprint) - Container: built from `eugr/spark-vllm-docker` recipe (TF5 lineage; same as the [forum-validated](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/qwen3-5-397b-a17b-run-in-dual-spark-but-i-have-a-concern/361967) Spark recipe) - PD firmware: `0x00000507` (post-fix for the [unrelated](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/359785) GX10 PD power-off bug — confirmed not the cause here; dmesg is clean) - Notable launch flags: `--max-model-len 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization-gb 110 --enable-prefix-caching --load-format instanttensor --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3` </details> ## 🐛 Describe the bug On a 2-node `--no-ray` vLLM serving setup, the head-node worker process **dies silently** after an extended idle period. The container stays "Up" because the API server process continues running briefly, but the engine is dead and all subsequent requests fail. **Specifically observed timeline (UTC):** | Time | Event | | --- | --- | | 09:15:56 | Last successful request completes. Engine 000 reports `Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%` | | 09:15:56 → 11:48:32 | **2 h 32 m of zero traffic.** No log entries on either node during this window. | | 11:48:32 | `(Worker_TP0 pid=193) WARNING multiproc_executor.py:884 WorkerProc was terminated` — no preceding error | | 11:48:45 | `(EngineCore pid=143) ERROR multiproc_executor.py:283 Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly, shutting down executor.` | | 11:48:46 | `RuntimeError: Executor failed.` → `vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError` → APIServer shutdown | | 12:45:04+ | On worker-rank-1 (gx10-node2): `ProcessGroupNCCL::HeartbeatMonitor::runLoop()` starts logging `TCPStore: sendBytes failed on SocketImpl(... remote=[192.168.0.72]:29501): Broken pipe` — rank 1's heartbeat monitor is trying to reach the dead head ~1 hour after the head's death | **Critical: no preceding NCCL/CUDA error log, no Xid in dmesg, no kernel OOM kill, no SIGTERM from container runtime.** The only log line at the moment of death is `WorkerProc was terminated` — which strongly suggests SIGABRT from PyTorch's own NCCL heartbeat watchdog rather than an out-of-band kill. ## Probable root cause `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` (default 600 s = 10 min) firing on a stuck `ProcessGroupNCCL::HeartbeatMonitor` thread. Mechanism: 1. PyTorch's `ProcessGroupNCCL::HeartbeatMonitor` runs as a separate thread polling the TCPStore. 2. Under extended idle on `--no-ray` distributed mode, the monitor thread's own poll can block (no fresh NCCL collectives to time against), and the watchdog SIGABRTs the worker process after `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` seconds with **no preceding NCCL error log**. 3. The 2 h 32 m idle window is far past the 600 s threshold. 4. The downstream rank-1 TCPStore broken-pipe storm exactly matches [pytorch/pytorch#123969](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/123969) (race where TCPStore is gone when heartbeat monitor calls `store->check()` after the master has shut down). ## Reproduction 1. Launch any large MoE on a 2-node ARM64 cluster (we hit it on dual GB10/GX10 but the mechanism should be hardware-independent) with `--no-ray --distributed-executor-backend ray -tp 2 --nnodes 2`. 2. Serve a few requests so the engine reaches warm steady state. 3. Stop sending requests for >10 minutes (we hit it after 2 h 32 m; theoretical kill window is 600 s). 4. Observe: head-node worker process disappears with `WorkerProc was terminated` as the only signal. EngineCore detects the dead worker on the next client request and raises `EngineDeadError`. ## Mitigation we're applying Added to the eugr recipe `env:` block: ```yaml env: TORCH_NCCL_ENABLE_MONITORING: 0 # disable the heartbeat watchdog SIGABRT TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC: 14400 # belt-and-suspenders: 4h ``` Trade-off: loses NCCL-deadlock auto-detection. For a controlled 2-node serving environment this is acceptable — we'd rather hang and be able to diagnose than have the process disappear with no log line. Will report back whether this prevents the recurrence. ## Adjacent issues - [vllm-project/vllm#41530](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41530) — TP-8 single-node `EngineDeadError` after ~1.5 h idle on DeepSeek-V4-Pro. Similar symptom chain (idle engine → dead worker → `EngineDeadError`) but the mechanism reported there is a shared-memory broadcast channel timeout, not a NCCL heartbeat kill. **Cross-referencing this issue.** - [pytorch/pytorch#123969](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/123969) — Race at shutdown where the TCPStore is gone when the heartbeat monitor calls `store->check()`. Matches the rank-1 broken-pipe storm we observed. - [pytorch/pytorch#163546](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/163546) — Better NCCL timeout handling. ## Question for maintainers 1. Is the `--no-ray` PyTorch distributed backend expected to keep NCCL collectives alive during long idle, or is the engine genuinely silent at the NCCL layer during idle? 2. If silent: should vLLM bake `TORCH_NCCL_ENABLE_MONITORING=0` (or a longer default `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC`) into the `--no-ray` launcher, or document the mitigation in the multi-node serving guide? 3. Is there a planned upstream fix to emit a clear log line when the heartbeat watchdog fires the SIGABRT, so this failure mode isn't silent next time? Happy to add `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` traces or test patches if useful.

signals.title: [Bug]: rejection sampler skips argmax-invariant procs — patching the min_p/logit_bias 400 alone is insufficient
signals.text: The guard at `vllm/sampling_params.py:_validate_spec_decode` 400s any spec-decode request with `min_p > _SAMPLING_EPS` or `logit_bias` set (added in #31982). Patching the raise out locally to let the params through reveals the underlying gap: the rejection sampler at `vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py:apply_logits_processors` only iterates `sampling_metadata.logitsprocs.non_argmax_invariant`. Both `MinPLogitsProcessor.is_argmax_invariant()` and `LogitBiasLogitsProcessor.is_argmax_invariant()` return `True` — the comment in `vllm/v1/sample/logits_processor/builtin.py` even says "Min-p never impacts greedy sampling". Net: even with the guard removed, min_p / logit_bias are NOT applied to verified target-logit tokens during rejection. They'd only land on bonus tokens via the regular Sampler path. Inconsistent honoring across a single response, arguably worse than the current 400 if a caller assumed they'd taken effect. Two ways to close this properly: 1. Mirror the regular Sampler in `apply_logits_processors` and include argmax-invariant procs (preserves determinism for greedy callers via the existing sampling_metadata check). 2. Route requests with `min_p`/`logit_bias` set to a non-spec target when they're present, leaving the guard as a hard fallback. ## Repro ``` vllm serve <model> --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":5}' curl /v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[...], "min_p":0.05}' # 400 BadRequest: "The min_p and logit_bias sampling parameters are not yet supported with speculative decoding." ``` ## Context Hitting this running `RedHatAI/Qwen3-Coder-Next-NVFP4` with ngram speculative decoding on a DGX Spark (GB10 / sm_121a) via the Avarok-Cybersecurity/dgx-vllm fork. Qwen-family AWQ/NVFP4 leans on `min_p` for repetition mitigation on code tasks -- without it (or equivalent), our diff-format outputs malform at ~80% rate. `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` are accepted via #19482 and partially compensate, but they aren't equivalent for this failure mode. ## Related - #31982 (the guard PR — added the 400) - #19482 (logit procs wired into rejection sampler — bad_words / penalties / allowed_token_ids only) - #18902 (older tracking issue, closed stale)
signals.author: camerono

signals.title: [Bug]: `apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch` `scatter_` crashes under cudagraph capture on sm_121a (Blackwell GB10)
signals.text: On a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121a) running vLLM 0.20.0 with speculative decoding enabled and the FlashInfer sampler unavailable, the PyTorch-native fallback `apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch` crashes the engine on any request with `top_p > 0` or `top_k > 0`: ``` torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted File "vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py", line 427 (main) / line 299 (v0.20.0), in apply_top_k_top_p_pytorch logits.scatter_(dim=-1, index=logits_idx, src=logits_sort) ``` The truncated text is the standard "operation not permitted when stream is capturing" — see pytorch/pytorch#87794. `cudagraph_mode` is already being downgraded to PIECEWISE under spec at startup (separate well-documented interaction), but the `scatter_` still ends up inside a captured region and faults. `EngineCoreError` cascades to 500s on subsequent requests, container exits. Why we hit the PyTorch-native fallback at all: FlashInfer's JIT-time arch detection rejects `sm_121a` (12.1a), so vLLM falls back. The Avarok-Cybersecurity/dgx-vllm fork patches FlashInfer for sm_121 in other modules but not in the sampler. ## Repro ``` docker run -e MODEL=<any nvfp4 model> ... \ vllm/vllm-openai \ ... --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":8}' # Send any request with top_p: 0.8, top_k: 20 — engine dies on first call. ``` ## Three potential fixes, in increasing depth 1. Replace the in-place `scatter_` with an out-of-place `torch.scatter(...)` into a pre-allocated buffer that's safe under cudagraph capture 2. Skip cudagraph capture for the sampler op specifically (the sampler shouldn't be the critical capture target anyway) 3. Make the FlashInfer sampler module actually loadable on sm_121a (root cause — would bypass this path entirely) ## Workarounds `--enforce-eager` or `cudagraph_mode=NONE` — both kill the crash at the cost of ~20-30% throughput. ## Related - #40742 (cudagraph memory profile crash with same root error) - pytorch/pytorch#87794 ("operation not permitted when stream is capturing") - #17898 (FlashInfer fallback warning) - #36821 (no sm_121 aarch64 support) - #31128 (Blackwell SM121 feature ticket)

signals.title: with_cancellation can return None, causing FastAPI to send HTTP 200 with JSON null after http.disconnect
signals.text: ## Summary The `with_cancellation` decorator in `vllm.entrypoints.utils` can return `None` when its `listen_for_disconnect()` task completes before the wrapped handler task. For FastAPI routes without an explicit response model or return annotation, FastAPI serializes that `None` return value as: ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: application/json content-length: 4 null ``` This is observable as intermittent empty/null successful responses, especially with large request bodies, keep-alive connections, concurrent requests, or request paths that take enough time for a spurious or premature `http.disconnect` event to win the race. I hit this in practice through `/v1/audio/transcriptions` with long audio uploads. The server accepted and logged the complete multipart upload, did not schedule any engine request, and returned `200` with body `null`. The client saw this as `aiohttp.ClientOSError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe`. ## Current Code Path Current `vllm/entrypoints/utils.py` still has: ```python done, pending = await asyncio.wait( [handler_task, cancellation_task], return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED ) for task in pending: task.cancel() if handler_task in done: return handler_task.result() return None ``` The final `return None` is the problematic path. This is especially visible on routes like `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, where the route handler has no return annotation and normally returns either `JSONResponse`, `StreamingResponse`, or an error response. ## Minimal Reproduction This reproducer does not require a model, GPU, uvicorn, a real TCP client, or any ASR/audio code. It directly invokes a tiny FastAPI ASGI app using the real `vllm.entrypoints.utils.with_cancellation`. Save this as `repro_vllm_with_cancellation_200_null.py`: ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import argparse import asyncio import json import sys from pathlib import Path def parse_args(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("--vllm-source", type=Path) parser.add_argument("--handler-delay", type=float, default=5.0) return parser.parse_args() def import_deps(vllm_source): if vllm_source is not None: sys.path.insert(0, str(vllm_source.resolve())) from fastapi import Body, FastAPI, Request from vllm.entrypoints.utils import with_cancellation return Body, FastAPI, Request, with_cancellation def make_app(handler_delay, deps): Body, FastAPI, Request, with_cancellation = deps # FastAPI resolves postponed/lazy annotations from globals. globals()["Request"] = Request app = FastAPI() @app.post("/repro") @with_cancellation async def repro_route( raw_request: Request, payload: dict[str, str] = Body(...), ): await asyncio.sleep(handler_delay) return {"ok": True, "payload": payload} return app async def call_app_with_disconnect(app): body = json.dumps({"message": "body was fully received"}).encode() request_messages = [ {"type": "http.request", "body": body, "more_body": False}, {"type": "http.disconnect"}, ] response_messages = [] scope = { "type": "http", "asgi": {"version": "3.0", "spec_version": "2.3"}, "http_version": "1.1", "method": "POST", "scheme": "http", "path": "/repro", "raw_path": b"/repro", "query_string": b"", "headers": [ (b"host", b"testserver"), (b"content-type", b"application/json"), (b"content-length", str(len(body)).encode()), ], "client": ("127.0.0.1", 12345), "server": ("testserver", 80), "root_path": "", } async def receive(): if request_messages: return request_messages.pop(0) return {"type": "http.disconnect"} async def send(message): response_messages.append(message) await app(scope, receive, send) return response_messages def response_from_messages(messages): status = None headers = [] body_parts = [] for message in messages: if message["type"] == "http.response.start": status = message["status"] headers = list(message.get("headers", [])) elif message["type"] == "http.response.body": body_parts.append(message.get("body", b"")) return status, b"".join(body_parts), headers async def main_async(): args = parse_args() app = make_app(args.handler_delay, import_deps(args.vllm_source)) messages = await call_app_with_disconnect(app) status, body, headers = response_from_messages(messages) print(f"status={status}") print(f"headers={[(k.decode(), v.decode()) for k, v in headers]}") print(f"body={body.decode('utf-8', 'replace')!r}") if status == 200 and body == b"null": print("BUG REPRODUCED: route returned HTTP 200 with JSON null.") else: print("BUG NOT REPRODUCED.") if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main_async()) ``` Run against an installed vLLM environment: ```bash python repro_vllm_with_cancellation_200_null.py ``` Or run against a source checkout: ```bash python repro_vllm_with_cancellation_200_null.py --vllm-source /path/to/vllm ``` ## Actual Output On a vLLM image based on `v0.20.2rc0-362-gf887aa1`, the script prints: ```text status=200 headers=[('content-length', '4'), ('content-type', 'application/json')] body='null' BUG REPRODUCED: route returned HTTP 200 with JSON null. ``` The same behavior is expected on current `origin/main` while `with_cancellation` still has the `return None` branch shown above. ## Expected Behavior If the client really disconnected, vLLM should not send a successful JSON `null` response. At minimum, `with_cancellation` should not return `None` from a wrapper whose decorated route handlers are expected to return response objects. A disconnected-client path should instead be represented as cancellation, for example: ```python raise asyncio.CancelledError("Client disconnected") ``` That matches the fix previously proposed in PR #32945. ## Real-World Failure Seen Through `/v1/audio/transcriptions` This bug was observed while sending long audio files to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. In one captured failure: ```text endpoint: /v1/audio/transcriptions client error: aiohttp.ClientOSError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe server response status: 200 server response body bytes: 4 server response body: null ``` The server-side HTTP debug middleware showed the failed request body was fully received: ```text request body_bytes: 150701092 request content_length: 150701092 response status_code: 200 response body_bytes: 4 response body: null ``` There were no server-side exceptions, no 4xx/5xx response, and no engine request was scheduled for that failed transcription request. Retrying the same audio file against the same server succeeded, so this was not a corrupt input file or a deterministic model failure. ## Why This Matters The response is semantically successful (`HTTP 200`) but contains no valid API response object. Clients may classify this as a successful request, a malformed response, or a transport-level write/read failure depending on timing and the HTTP client implementation. For `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, this can silently drop long requests before model execution while surfacing as confusing client-side upload errors. ## Related Issues and PRs ### PR #32945: likely same root cause, closed unmerged <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/32945> PR #32945 appears to diagnose and fix this exact root cause: - `with_cancellation` returns `None` when the disconnect listener wins. - FastAPI serializes `None` as a successful empty/null response. - The proposed fix changes `return None` to `raise asyncio.CancelledError("Client disconnected")`. - It adds regression tests around `with_cancellation` and concurrent empty responses. However, the PR is closed and not merged: ```text state: CLOSED mergedAt: null mergeCommit: null ``` I also checked that the PR head is not an ancestor of current `origin/main`, and `origin/main` still has the `return None` branch. ### Issue #3209: symptom-related, older, not the same root cause <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/3209> Issue #3209 reported HTTP 200 responses with empty output under concurrent load. It is symptom-related, and PR #32945 mentions it, but the issue predates the current `with_cancellation` implementation and was closed after discussion of prompt/model behavior. It does not contain the deterministic `with_cancellation`/`http.disconnect` root cause described here. ### Issue #10087 and PR #11190: introduced the current cancellation wrapper <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/10087> <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/11190> Issue #10087 reported that request cancellation did not work reliably with middleware. PR #11190 fixed that by introducing the current `with_cancellation` decorator and the `listen_for_disconnect()` race pattern. That solved the middleware polling problem, but the `return None` branch in the new wrapper creates the successful-null-response failure described here. ### Issue #13757: transcription endpoint issue, likely unrelated <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/13757> This issue also involves `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `with_cancellation`, but it is about FastAPI form parsing / missing request fields. It does not appear to be the same `HTTP 200 null` cancellation failure. ## Proposed Fix Direction The smallest fix appears to be the same core change proposed in #32945: ```diff if handler_task in done: return handler_task.result() -return None +raise asyncio.CancelledError("Client disconnected") ``` It would also be useful to add a focused ASGI-level regression test similar to the minimal reproducer above: 1. Build a tiny FastAPI app with a `@with_cancellation` route. 2. Send a complete request body. 3. Then send `http.disconnect`. 4. Assert the app does not emit `HTTP 200` with body `null`. This test does not need a model, engine, GPU, OpenAI client, or real network server.

Public repo; ships no remote code (no `auto_map` / modeling `.py`). ### The closest model vLLM already supports. vLLM registers `Gemma4ForCausalLM` and `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, but **not** the `Unified` variant. The supported-models docs list only `Gemma4ForCausalLM`. ### What happens today. Serving fails at model load, before any request: ValueError: The checkpoint you are trying to load has model type gemma4_unified but Transformers does not recognize this architecture. Verified in-image: - `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` is **absent** from `ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs()`. - `gemma4_unified` is **absent** from `transformers` `CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES`. - No remote code in the repo, so `--trust-remote-code` does not help. ### Request. Add `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` to vLLM's model registry, and document the minimum `transformers` version that provides the `gemma4_unified` config.

signals.title: [Bug]: MLA chunked-context prefill crashes on sm80 with Marlin FP8: kv_c_normed cast to packed-int32 weight dtype (`unsupported \`a\` scalar_type`)
signals.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM 0.23.0 (official image), PyTorch 2.x, Triton, NCCL 2.28.9 - 12× NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (compute capability **8.0**, no native FP8) across 3 nodes - Model: GLM-5.2-FP8 (fp8 weights → `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` / `MARLIN Fp8 MoE`), PP=3 × TP=4, `--enable-expert-parallel` - Attention: `TRITON_MLA` decode backend, `FLASH_ATTN` MLA prefill backend, bf16 KV cache - (We run with sparse attention disabled via a local patch because of #35021, but this bug is in the generic MLA chunked-context path and should reproduce with any fp8 MLA model on sm80, e.g. DeepSeek-V3/R1-FP8 on A100.) ### 🐛 Describe the bug On sm80 with fp8 weights (Marlin), any request that takes the **chunked-context prefill path** — i.e. a prefix-cache hit or a prompt longer than `max_num_batched_tokens` — crashes the worker with: ``` RuntimeError: unsupported `a` scalar_type ``` in `torch.ops._C.marlin_gemm`, called from `kv_b_proj` inside `MLACommonImpl._compute_prefill_context`. Requests that don't hit that path (short prompts, no shared prefix, plain decode) work fine, so the server passes startup, warmup, and simple smoke tests, then dies on the first prefix-cache hit in real traffic. **Root cause** — `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`, in `_compute_prefill_context`: ```python _kv_b_proj_w_dtype = ( self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype if hasattr(self.kv_b_proj, "weight") else self.kv_b_proj.params_dtype ) if ( use_fp8_prefill or _kv_b_proj_w_dtype != current_platform.fp8_dtype() ) and _kv_b_proj_w_dtype != torch.uint8: kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype) ``` The intent is "cast the gathered KV back to the layer's expected input dtype, except for quantized layouts". But on sm80, `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.process_weights_after_loading` repacks the fp8 weight via `pack_fp8_to_int32` + `gptq_marlin_repack` and `replace_parameter(layer, "weight", marlin_qweight)` — so `kv_b_proj.weight.dtype` is **`torch.int32`** (packed), not `float8_e4m3fn`. The condition (`!= fp8_dtype()`, `!= uint8`) doesn't exclude it, so the bf16 activations are cast to `torch.int32` and `marlin_gemm` rejects them. On Hopper the weight stays fp8 so the cast is skipped and nothing breaks, which is presumably why this wasn't caught. ### Reproduction 1. Serve any fp8-quantized MLA model on an sm80 GPU (Marlin path), with prefix caching enabled (default). 2. Send one short request. It succeeds. 3. Send a second request sharing a token prefix with the first (or a single prompt longer than `max_num_batched_tokens`). 4. Worker crashes with the traceback below; engine core dies. ### Traceback (trimmed) ``` File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 2300, in forward_mha context_output, context_lse = self._compute_prefill_context( File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 2097, in _compute_prefill_context kv_nope = self.kv_b_proj(kv_c_normed)[0].view( File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 582, in forward output_parallel = self.quant_method.apply(self, input_, bias) File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 474, in apply return self.fp8_linear.apply_weights(layer, x, bias) File ".../vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/marlin.py", line 114, in apply_weights return apply_fp8_marlin_linear( File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp8.py", line 69, in apply_fp8_marlin_linear output = ops.marlin_gemm( RuntimeError: unsupported `a` scalar_type ``` ### Suggested fix Only perform the cast when the target dtype is a floating-point type — for packed integer weight layouts (Marlin int32, NVFP4 uint8, …) the quant method expects model-dtype input and quantizes internally, exactly like the normal (non-context) prefill path already does: ```python if ( (use_fp8_prefill or _kv_b_proj_w_dtype != current_platform.fp8_dtype()) and _kv_b_proj_w_dtype != torch.uint8 and _kv_b_proj_w_dtype.is_floating_point ): kv_c_normed = kv_c_normed.to(self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype) ``` (The existing `!= torch.uint8` special case then becomes redundant.) We've been running this fix in production on 12×A100 and it resolves the crash: prefix-cache hits and 6.5K-token chunked prefills work, outputs are correct. Happy to send a PR if the approach looks right. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the documentation and examples.

### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... uv is set ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Linux Mint 22.1 (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : Could not collect Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu128 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 12.8 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-6.8.0-134-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 12.0.140 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU Nvidia driver version : 580.159.03 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.1.dev18413+g6569df6a3 (git sha: 6569df6a3) vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: Not Set; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ```
Note: this bug is in pure Python config-derivation logic (`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`) and is independent of GPU/driver/topology. It affects any multi-node **hybrid data-parallel load balancing** deployment (`docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md`, "Hybrid Load Balancing" section), regardless of hardware. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary:** When a node explicitly passes `--data-parallel-start-rank 0`, `EngineArgs.create_engine_config` treats it identically to "not specified," because the field is checked with Python truthiness (`if self.data_parallel_start_rank`) instead of `is not None`. Since `0` is a perfectly valid and meaningful starting rank (the node owning the first slice of ranks), this silently corrupts the derived `data_parallel_hybrid_lb` flag for exactly that node. #### The two buggy lines `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`, inside `create_engine_config`: ```python # line 1997 if self.data_parallel_start_rank and not headless: # Infer hybrid LB mode. self.data_parallel_hybrid_lb = True ``` ```python # line 2016 self.data_parallel_rank = ( self.data_parallel_start_rank or inferred_data_parallel_rank ) ``` In both cases, `self.data_parallel_start_rank == 0` is falsy, so: - Line 1997: the condition is `0 and not headless` → `False`, so `self.data_parallel_hybrid_lb` is **never inferred `True`** for this node, even though the deployment doc explicitly requires hybrid LB nodes to pass `--data-parallel-start-rank` so "each node knows which ranks it owns" (`docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md`, lines 87-91) — including the node that owns rank 0. - Line 2016: `0 or inferred_data_parallel_rank` evaluates to `inferred_data_parallel_rank`. This usually happens to still resolve to `0` in the common single-process-per-node case, but it means the explicit user-supplied value is discarded in favor of a derived one, which is fragile and wrong in intent even when the numeric result coincides. #### The correct pattern already exists 27 lines above, for the sibling field ```python # line 1969 — data_parallel_rank, handled correctly data_parallel_external_lb = ( self.data_parallel_external_lb or self.data_parallel_rank is not None ) ``` This is the established, correct convention in this exact function for exactly this class of field (`int | None`, where `0` is a valid value). The two other places in the codebase that read `data_parallel_start_rank` also use `is not None` correctly: - `vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py:86`: `is_hybrid_lb = args.data_parallel_start_rank is not None` - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/dp_supervisor.py:39-40`: `if start_rank is not None: return start_rank` Neither of those call sites compensates for the bug, though — `serve.py`'s `is_hybrid_lb` is a local variable used only for `--api-server-count` defaulting and LB-mode mutual-exclusivity checks; it is never written back to `args.data_parallel_hybrid_lb`. `dp_supervisor.py` is a separate code path (multi-port external LB) that never touches `data_parallel_hybrid_lb`. So `arg_utils.py:1997`/`2016` are the only place that derive `self.data_parallel_hybrid_lb` from this flag, and they get it wrong specifically for rank 0. #### Downstream impact chain The corrupted `data_parallel_hybrid_lb` flag propagates into `ParallelConfig.data_parallel_hybrid_lb` and is consumed in multiple places: 1. `vllm/config/parallel.py:536`, `ParallelConfig.local_engines_only`: ```python return self.data_parallel_external_lb or self.data_parallel_hybrid_lb ``` For the rank-0 node in a hybrid-LB deployment, this wrongly evaluates to `False` instead of `True`. 2. `vllm/v1/engine/utils.py:1244`, `wait_for_engine_startup`: ```python remote_should_be_headless = ( not parallel_config.data_parallel_hybrid_lb and not parallel_config.data_parallel_external_lb ) ``` Wrongly evaluates to `True` for that node, misclassifying the expected startup behavior of remote engines. 3. `vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py`, in the Rust-frontend startup path added by #45805 (merged 2026-06-17): ```python if parallel_config.local_engines_only: expected_engine_start_index = parallel_config.data_parallel_rank expected_engine_count = parallel_config.data_parallel_size_local else: expected_engine_start_index = 0 expected_engine_count = parallel_config.data_parallel_size ``` Because `local_engines_only` is wrongly `False` for the rank-0 node, the Rust frontend computes it as owning **all** global engines (`0`, `data_parallel_size`) instead of just its local slice (`data_parallel_rank`, `data_parallel_size_local`). None of these downstream consumers compensate for or work around the truthiness bug — they all trust `data_parallel_hybrid_lb` as computed in `arg_utils.py`. #### Steps to reproduce Set up a 2-node hybrid load-balancing deployment per `docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md` ("Hybrid Load Balancing"): ```bash # Node 0 (owns global ranks 0-1, i.e. the first slice) — non-headless, exposes its own API endpoint vllm serve $MODEL --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 2 \ --data-parallel-start-rank 0 \ --data-parallel-address 192.0.2.1 --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 # Node 1 (owns global ranks 2-3) vllm serve $MODEL --headless --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size-local 2 \ --data-parallel-start-rank 2 \ --data-parallel-address 192.0.2.1 --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 ``` Node 0 (rank 0) ends up misclassified as not participating in hybrid LB while every other node in the same deployment is classified correctly — see the minimal reproduction below for the exact config values this produces. #### Minimal reproduction (no cluster required) The same underlying bug can be triggered directly against `EngineArgs.create_engine_config`, without standing up an actual multi-node deployment: ```python from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs from vllm.usage.usage_lib import UsageContext engine_args = EngineArgs( model="facebook/opt-125m", data_parallel_size=4, data_parallel_size_local=2, data_parallel_start_rank=0, ) vllm_config = engine_args.create_engine_config(UsageContext.OPENAI_API_SERVER) print("data_parallel_hybrid_lb:", vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_hybrid_lb) print("data_parallel_rank:", vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_rank) ``` Actual output on current `main` (commit `6569df6a3`): ``` data_parallel_hybrid_lb: False data_parallel_rank: 0 ``` Expected output (and what this snippet produces once `data_parallel_start_rank` is checked with `is not None` instead of truthiness): ``` data_parallel_hybrid_lb: True data_parallel_rank: 0 ``` ### Proposed fix Use `is not None` instead of truthiness at both sites, matching the existing convention used for the sibling field `data_parallel_rank` (line 1969) and the other two call sites of this same field (`serve.py:86`, `dp_supervisor.py:40`): ```python # line 1997 if self.data_parallel_start_rank is not None and not headless: self.data_parallel_hybrid_lb = True ``` ```python # line 2016 self.data_parallel_rank = ( self.data_parallel_start_rank if self.data_parallel_start_rank is not None else inferred_data_parallel_rank ) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [RFC]: StructuredOutputManager x Speculative Decoding Refactor
signals.text: ### Motivation. Simplify the contract between `Scheduler`, grammar backend, and `StructuredOutputManager`, especially when speculative decoding is used. `StructuredOutputManager` exists because constrained decoding often doesn't kick in until a model has finished reasoning. With speculative decoding, grammar-invalid draft tokens need to be rejected, draft tokens need to temporarily advance grammar state to generate bitmasks, rejected draft tokens should not advance grammar state. Reasoning end boundary can also fall in the middle of the draft token window, so only draft tokens after said boundary should advance grammar state. `Scheduler` and the `StructuredOutputManager` need to do a careful dance to make this is all correct. This leads to some bugs such as [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) -- only recently fixed thanks to [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297). ``` Per request inside a scheduler step 1. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request) # Should we constrain some draft tokens? Grammar.validate_tokens(draft tokens) # Reject grammar invalid draft tokens 2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...) # Generate bitmasks for the draft tokens 3. Verifier runs 4. StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request) # Should we constrain some draft token? StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens) # Trim the draft tokens that are not constrained Grammar.accept_tokens(verified tokens) # Advance grammar state ``` In fact, speculative decoding x constrained decoding remains fragile / subtly incorrect: 1. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` treats STRUCTURAL_TAG vs other constraint types differently. It defers non STRUCTURAL_TAG constraints. [#44297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297) only fix the strict tool calling case (which uses STRUCTURAL_TAG); [#34650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34650) is still unfixed for JSON, REGEX, and other constraint types.~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993 2. ~~`StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` also doesn't answer "should we constrain some draft tokens?" reliably. It incorrectly infers the draft token window from `num_output_placeholders`. ~~ Fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44993 3. `Grammar.validate_tokens(draft_tokens)` only works on a best effort basis -- it doesn't validate any draft token unless all draft tokens should be constrained. We rely on `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...)` and rejection sampling to discard grammer-invalid tokens. ### Proposed Change. Let `StructuredOutputManager` handle the token validation and grammar advancement. Remove: - `StructuredOutputManager.should_advance(request)` - `StructuredOutputManager.trim_reasoning_for_advance(verified tokens)` Add: - `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens)` - `StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens)` ``` Per request inside a scheduler step 1. StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens(draft tokens) 2. StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask(...) 3. Verifier runs 4. StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens(verified tokens) ``` Internally, `validate_tokens()`, `grammar_bitmask()`, and `accept_tokens()` all use the same `_get_constraint_start()` helper to determine whether and where draft tokens should be constrained and grammar state advanced. Concretly, `_get_constraint_start()` computes the first token that should be grammar-constrained. - `validate_tokens()` preserves any unconstrained prefix and validates only the constrained suffix. - `grammar_bitmask()` emits unconstrained bitmaks before the boundary and constrained bitmasks after it. - `accept_tokens()` advances the grammar state only on the constrained suffix only This gives a simpler mental model for the system. The scheduler is responsible for request lifecycle and token plumbing. `StructuredOutputManager` is responsible for draft token validation, bitmask generation, and grammar backends. ~100 insertions, ~200 deletions of changes excluding test updates. Would fix issues like: #34650 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43388 ### CC List. @njhill @mgoin @chaunceyjiang @benchislett @arpera ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 tool-call parser leaks raw DSML into content when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START token (long context)
signals.text: ## Summary On **DeepSeek-V4-Flash**, at long input context (~95k+ tokens), the model intermittently **omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper token** while still emitting a well-formed `<｜DSML｜invoke ...>…</｜DSML｜invoke>` block. `deepseekv32_tool_parser.py` (inherited by V4) anchors tool-call detection **solely on the exact START-token string**, so when it is missing the entire invoke block is returned as plain assistant `content` (raw DSML leak) and **no `tool_calls` are produced**. Occurs in both non-streaming and streaming paths. Clients then hang because the tool call is delivered as text. ## Environment - vLLM `0.1.dev17209` (2026-07-01 build) - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tensor-parallel TP=2 - Flags: `--tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4` - `--default-chat-template-kwargs {"thinking":false}` (reasoning parser falls back to Identity) ## Root cause - **Non-streaming** `extract_tool_calls` (`deepseekv32_tool_parser.py`, ~L186-189): `if self.tool_call_start_token not in model_output: return ExtractedToolCallInformation(tools_called=False, ..., content=model_output)` — a complete invoke/parameter/END sequence is ignored when the START token is absent. - **Streaming** `_process_streaming_buffer` (~L403-421): in the `not _in_tool_calls` state it emits the buffer as content until the START token appears; if it never comes, the whole block leaks. - The START omission is a **model behavior at long context**, documented in `vllm/reasoning/deepseek_v4_reasoning_parser.py` docstring (the model may skip `</think>` and open `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>`); the same skipping affects the tool_calls START token. - **Out of scope of #41240 / #41801 / #40800-40801**: those addressed `string="true"` attribute handling, wrapper repair, and streaming flush of *split* markers. This is a **complete START-token omission**, not a split/edge-case marker. ## Reproduction (parser-level, no GPU) Feed a complete invoke block **without** the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper (the END token may or may not be present): ``` <｜DSML｜invoke name="terminal"><｜DSML｜parameter name="command" string="true">echo hi</｜DSML｜parameter></｜DSML｜invoke></｜DSML｜tool_calls> ``` `extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)` → `tools_called=False`, `content` = the raw DSML above. Prepending `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` makes the identical payload parse into a valid `terminal` tool call. Verified byte-for-byte against a real user leak. ## Suggested fix (orphan-invoke fallback) When the START token is absent **but** a *complete* `<｜DSML｜invoke …>…</｜DSML｜invoke>` block exists: - **non-streaming**: synthesize the missing START/END wrapper around the invoke span, then run the normal wrapper-based parse (return `None`/plain content if no complete invoke block exists — prose merely mentioning the marker is never misparsed); - **streaming**: enter tool mode only on a *full* `invoke_start_regex` match, with bounded hold-back plus an **EOS safety valve** that retains only in-progress marker bytes so no content is silently swallowed on a mis-detected stream end (note `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` is 6 ordinary BPE tokens, not a single special token, so a multi-token marker can span an empty mid-stream delta). I currently run this as a local patch (68 regression checks incl. mid-stream empty-delta and multi-invoke; normal START-present traffic is byte-identical). Happy to open a PR if maintainers agree on the approach.
